prompt:
# Subject Merge Fine Clustering

## Quick Start

Inside one topic area, create tight candidate clusters that are worth a later same-concept decision. Use only the provided candidate cards.

## Identity Filter

Cluster candidates only when they might be the same teachable idea at the same level, testable with the same question.

Do not cluster just because candidates share a keyword. Keep candidates separate when one adds implementation, math, limitation, application, deeper mechanism, tool-specific behavior, or a broader/narrower student action.

Doubt means singleton. Under-clustering is safer than sending unrelated candidates to merge evaluation.

## Output

Return one JSON object only:

```json
{
  "clusters": [
    {
      "id": "cluster_001",
      "label": "Short candidate cluster",
      "rationale": "Why these candidates may share concept identity.",
      "candidate_ids": ["candidate-id"]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Self-Check

- Every input candidate ID appears exactly once.
- Each non-singleton cluster has a plausible same-concept reason.
- Implementation, limitation, application, math, and deeper-revisit candidates were not grouped with definitions just because labels overlap.
- Mixed-language same-level candidates were clustered when their teachable idea matches.
- No web search or external knowledge was used.

area.label: Latent Semantic Analysis
area.rationale: LSA definition, document-term matrix, SVD, and NLP vocabulary for topic modeling.

candidates.label: NLP Vocabulary: Document, Body, Dictionary, Topic
candidates.description: In NLP, a document is a single data instance (e.g., a paragraph, tweet). The body (or corpus) is the collection of all documents. The dictionary is the set of all unique words occurring in at least one document. A topic is a collection of co-occurring words that represent a theme.
coverage_criteria: Define the terms document, body (corpus), dictionary, and topic in NLP.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: Latent Semantic Analysis (LSA) Definition
candidates.description: LSA is an unsupervised NLP technique that discovers latent topics in a corpus by applying dimensionality reduction (via SVD) to the document-term matrix, yielding lower-dimensional encodings of documents as combinations of topics.
coverage_criteria: Explain what LSA is and its purpose in text analysis.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: Document-Term Matrix in LSA
candidates.description: A document-term matrix is a representation where rows correspond to documents, columns to dictionary words, and cells indicate word presence or frequency. It serves as the input to SVD in LSA.
coverage_criteria: Describe the structure of a document-term matrix.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidates.label: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) in LSA
candidates.description: In LSA, Singular Value Decomposition is applied to the document-term matrix to reduce its dimensionality and extract latent topics, analogous to PCA. This transforms the high-dimensional word space into a lower-dimensional topic space.
coverage_criteria: State the role of SVD in LSA and its analogy to PCA.
candidates.lesson_title: Outras técnicas Word Embedding: TF, TF-IDF e LSA

candidate_assignment_rule: Cluster only. Every input candidate ID must appear exactly once across clusters. Prefer tight clusters; topic overlap alone is not a cluster.

web_access_policy.instruction: Do not use web search or open URLs. Use only the provided candidate cards.
